prompt: Break each month's MRR movements down by kind. For each month of 2025 (event_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025) with at least one movement event, give the new, expansion, reactivation, contraction and churn MRR in euros, each signed as in mrr_delta_local, so contraction and churn are negative. Each event's event_type names its movement (new, expansion, contraction, churn or reactivation); a reactivation is an account coming back after it churned, never new MRR. Leave out the opening events: they carry the MRR subscriptions already had when the data starts on 1 January 2024. Convert every amount to euros at one fixed rate, that of 31 December 2025: multiply by fx_rates.eur_per_unit for the subscription's currency on 2025-12-31. Count an event in the month of its event_date. A kind with no event that month shows 0. Round each to 2 decimals with ROUND. Return six columns, in this order: month_start, new_mrr, expansion_mrr, reactivation_mrr, contraction_mrr and churn_mrr. Return one row for each such month. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per month of 2025 with a movement event

hints: Next, write one conditional sum for each kind of movement.
One CASE per column picks its own event_type; the opening events are already gone in the CTE.
faded_shape:
WITH moves AS (
  -- one row per movement event in 2025, in euros
  SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', e.event_date) AS DATE) AS month_start, e.event_type,
    e.mrr_delta_local * f.eur_per_unit AS mrr_eur
  FROM subscription_events e
  JOIN subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = e.subscription_id
  JOIN fx_rates f ON f.currency = s.currency AND f.rate_date = DATE '2025-12-31'
  WHERE e.event_type <> 'opening'
    AND e.event_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
)
SELECT month_start,
why_this_works: Conditional sums put each event in the column of its own movement, so the five columns add up to the month's net change.
